mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 7.5% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during episodes where GDPC1 YoY < -2% and UNRATE > 7.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 100,000 persons for four consecutive months signals labor market strength, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥100,000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods of four consecutive months with monthly PAYEMS increases ≥100,000.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) of at least 0.5% signals robust demand expansion, which supports corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 0.5% AND HOUST > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during months where GDPC1 and HOUST both rise by > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 1% and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising above 2% for three consecutive months, it signals a low-rate, high-inflation regime that erodes real yields and boosts equities, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL > 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL > 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for six consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and cost margins, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as profit growth slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of six consecutive months with UNRATE < 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for four consecutive months, regardless of other conditions, signals weakening consumer demand and is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of four consecutive months with RSAFS declines > 1%.
